t.en: So far you have chosen the sentences on parts yourself: what a box assumes, which side Add alternative adds. Often the goal already says what goes there.

A rule can be written with blanks: Join is ⟦?A; ?B⟧ ⟹ ?A ∧ ?B, the premises in brackets, the conclusion after ⟹. ?A and ?B are <wiki-ref to="metavariable"></wiki-ref>s. The notation is <wiki-ref to="isabelle"></wiki-ref>’s; <wiki-ref to="lean"></wiki-ref> has metavariables too.

To use a rule on a goal, its conclusion must first fit the goal: solve ?A ∧ ?B ≐ it rains ∧ it is windy for ?A and ?B. This is <wiki-ref to="unification"></wiki-ref>. A new part, “Decompose”, splits an equation whose sides share a shape into equations between corresponding parts.

brief.en: Design a proof assistant that fits a rule’s conclusion to a goal, splitting until each equation has a single ?-letter on its left.

hint.en: One Decompose splits one level. The third test has two.
